physical: Data processing inequality — Processing cannot increase information: if Z depends on X only through Y, then the information Z carries about X is at most what Y carries. I(X;Z) ≤ I(X;Y). Form: inequality.
reflected_sentence: The bound keeps its shape: what the last in a chain can say about the first never exceeds what the middle can say — stated in plain words, because this carried-aboutness has no partner in the frozen vocabulary.
rule_reason: the limit (at-most) is set by the ordering of dependence X to Y to Z, not by any resistance-carrying quantity; no resistance-cost and no separation, zero (even) keeps the shape
unmapped_terms: the chain of dependence X -> Y -> Z
interpretation: Nothing crosses. The bound keeps its shape in silence.
closing: An inequality looks like a limit, and limits caused by resistance turn, so I checked what sets this bound. It is set by the dependence structure, and mutual information is pre-decided as a measure, not resistance. The fixed table made that check mechanical, so no judgment call was needed on the shape.
